registered: 2026-10-07, before any computation (Test Lead: estimate motor's quiz power on public data before the owner decides)

near_band.status: HUMAN_INPUT recommendation (10 % of each limit); used here only to size the stand-in

q2.batch: each draw: a random half of the pool
q2.selection: random from the near-band cases of the batch

q3.pool: pseudo-scenarios: every 4-design subset of study V2's 8 designs at its 6 conditions (the only public complete grid; 70 subsets), all-infeasible subsets excluded
q3.rule: V2 decision rule: feasible iff every condition meets both limits; minimise worst-condition ripple fraction, ties to higher worst mean torque; abstain if none predicted feasible

known_bad: boundary_optimist: within the near band, mean +0.5 N m and ripple x 0.8
localized_sign_error: within 0.4 N m of the torque limit, mean reflected about 4.0
infeasible_edge_seeker: where truly infeasible within the near band, reports just passing (mean 4.001, ripple fraction 0.299)
known_good_standin: oracle plus 9 noisy oracles (multiplicative lognormal noise, sigma 3 % on mean torque and 10 % on ripple pk-pk, seeds 0-8): a STAND-IN construction, not a recorded value, because motor has only two real models
value_control: near_limit_cautious (the optimist's mirror), reported as over-caution
metric: AUC over 1000 draws (numpy PCG64, seed 20261007): P(measure of known-bad > measure of known-good); mean and 5th percentile. Q2 measure: false-feasible; Q3 measure: decision false-feasible

pooling.option: a hotkey's quiz verdict pools its outcomes over its last W batches (same construction identity only)
pooling.stand_in: power reported at effective sizes n x W and k x W

cadence: AX42, 16 threads; GetDP at 2 CPUs per case, so 8 concurrent; median 1,366 s per case (counted campaign)
